scenes.title: The biggest stone ever cut
scenes.text: See the tiny person? These are the biggest stone blocks known from the ancient world, and they never left the quarry.

scenes.title: Baalbek, Lebanon
scenes.text: This is Baalbek, Lebanon, and its giant Roman Temple of Jupiter.

scenes.title: Giant columns
scenes.text: Six columns still stand, each about twenty metres tall.

scenes.title: The trilithon
scenes.text: In its base: the trilithon, three blocks of about eight hundred tonnes each.

scenes.title: Stone of the Pregnant Woman
scenes.text: In the quarry lies the Stone of the Pregnant Woman: about a thousand tonnes, never moved.

scenes.title: An even bigger one
scenes.text: In 2014, archaeologists found a bigger one beside it: about sixteen hundred and fifty tonnes.

scenes.title: How did they do it?
scenes.text: Most archaeologists credit Roman engineers, with ramps, rollers and capstans, from a quarry just uphill.

scenes.title: Still debated
scenes.text: But exactly how the trilithon was lifted is still debated.
